title: 2014 USAMO Problem 5
statement: Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with orthocenter \(H\) and let \(P\) be the second intersection of the circumcircle of triangle \(AHC\) with the internal bisector of the angle \(\angle BAC\). Let \(X\) be the circumcenter of triangle \(APB\) and \(Y\) the orthocenter of triangle \(APC\). Prove that the length of segment \(XY\) is equal to the circumradius of triangle \(ABC\).

solutions.text:
Let $O_1$ be the center of $(AHPC)$, $O$ be the center of $(ABC)$. Note that $(O_1)$ is the reflection of $(O)$ across $AC$, so $AO=AO_1$. Additionally
\[\angle AYC=180-\angle APC=180-\angle AHC=\angle B\]
so $Y$ lies on $(O)$. Now since $XO,OO_1,XO_1$ are perpendicular to $AB,AC,$ and their bisector, $XOO_1$ is isosceles with $XO=OO_1$, and $\angle XOO_1=180-\angle A$. Also
\[\angle AOY=2\angle ACY=2(90-\angle PAC)=2(90-\frac{A}{2})=180-\angle A = \angle XOO_1\]
But $YO=OA$ as well, and $\angle YOX=\angle AOO_1$, so $\triangle OYX\cong \triangle OAO_1$. Thus $XY=AO_1=AO$.
